note: Links a describer to a noun, like 's or 'of': 我的 wǒ de 'my', 好吃的菜 hǎo chī de cài 'tasty food'. Other readings: dí in 的確 dí què 'indeed', dì in 目的 mù dì 'goal'.
Links two nouns (A 是 shì B). Not used before adjectives: say 我很累 wǒ hěn lèi, not 我是累 wǒ shì lèi. A bare 是 shì for 'yes' sounds formal; everyday Taiwan speech uses 對 duì or 嗯 en.

After a verb it marks a finished action (我吃了 wǒ chī le 'I ate'); at the end of a sentence it marks a new situation (下雨了 xià yǔ le 'it's raining now'). Other reading liǎo 'to finish', as in 受不了 shòu bu liǎo 'can't stand it'.
Says where someone or something is (他在家 tā zài jiā 'he's at home'). Before a verb it means 'in the middle of': 我在吃飯 wǒ zài chī fàn 'I'm eating'.
Negates habits, wishes and the present/future (我不去 wǒ bù qù 'I'm not going'). Use 沒 méi for 有 yǒu and for things that didn't happen. Spoken bú before a 4th tone: 不要 bú yào.
In speech tā covers he and she. In writing 'she' is 她 tā and 'it' is 它 tā/牠 tā, all pronounced tā; in speech 'it' is usually left out or said with 這 zhè/那 nà.
Negated with 沒 méi (沒有 méi yǒu 'don't have'), never 不有 bù yǒu. Taiwan Mandarin also uses 有 yǒu before a verb for 'did': 我有去 wǒ yǒu qù 'I did go'.
Taiwan uses 我們 wǒ men for every 'we'; the mainland 咱們 zán men ('we, including you') is rarely heard.

hint: as in 'this is…'; before a measure word
note: Used alone (這是 zhè shì… 'this is…') or before a number/measure word (這個 zhè ge, 這次 zhè cì). Before a measure word it is often said zhèi: 這個 zhèi ge.

hint: as soon as; sooner than expected
note: Very flexible adverb: 'then / as soon as' (吃完就走 chī wán jiù zǒu 'leave right after eating'), 'exactly' (就是他 jiù shì tā 'it's him'), 'only' (就一個 jiù yī ge 'just one').

example.english: There are so many people here.

note: Joins nouns, not sentences. Many Taiwanese say hàn (an MOE-listed colloquial reading), and in casual speech 跟 gēn is more common. Other readings: hè in 附和 fù hè 'to echo', huò in 和麵 huò miàn 'to knead dough' (MOE; the mainland says huó), and hú (winning in mahjong).

example.pinyin: Bàba hé māma dōu zài jiā.
example.english: Mom and Dad are both home.

note: Added to the end of a statement to make a yes/no question: 你好 nǐ hǎo → 你好嗎 nǐ hǎo ma? Don't use it with question words like 什麼 shén me or 誰 shéi.

A learned skill (我會游泳 wǒ huì yóu yǒng 'I can swim') or what is likely to happen (明天會下雨 míng tiān huì xià yǔ 'it will rain tomorrow'). Compare 能 néng (able) and 可以 kě yǐ (allowed). Other reading kuài in 會計 kuài jì 'accountant'.
Taiwanese often use 講 jiǎng for the same meaning in casual speech. Other reading shuì in 遊說 yóu shuì 'to lobby'.
Alone it means 'okay / sure'. Before an adjective it means 'so, really' (好累 hǎo lèi 'so tired'), very common in Taiwan. Other reading hào 'to be fond of' (愛好 ài hào).

gloss: to want; to need to; will
note: More direct than 想 xiǎng. Also 'need to / should' (你要小心 nǐ yào xiǎo xīn 'be careful') and 'about to' (要下雨了 yào xià yǔ le). Other reading yāo in 要求 yāo qiú 'to demand'.

example.english: What would you like to drink?

note: Goes before the verb and sums up the people or things already mentioned: 我們都去 wǒ men dōu qù 'we're all going'. Other reading dū 'capital city' (首都 shǒu dū).
Goes before the verb, never at the end: 我也是 wǒ yě shì 'me too'.
In fast Taiwan speech it often sounds like shé me.
Also 'let me / I'll do it' before a verb (我來 wǒ lái 'let me'), and after verbs for movement toward the speaker (拿來 ná lái 'bring here').
Alone it means 'yes, right'. As a preposition it means 'to / toward': 他對我很好 tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo 'he's good to me'. Also counts pairs: 一對 yī duì 'a pair'.
Tone changes in speech: yí before a 4th tone (一個 yí ge), yì before other tones (一起 yì qǐ), yī when counting or at the end.
Often just links a subject and an adjective without much 'very': 我很好 wǒ hěn hǎo 'I'm fine'.
The default measure word, used for people and most things that lack a special one: 一個人 yī ge rén, 兩個問題 liǎng ge wèn tí. Usually unstressed in speech (ge).
Also 'to (a place)' (到台北 dào tái běi 'to Taipei') and 'until' (到明天 dào míng tiān). After a verb it means you succeeded: 找到 zhǎo dào 'found', 看到 kàn dào 'saw'.
A place word: 桌上 zhuō shàng 'on the table'. As a verb 'to go up / get on / attend': 上車 shàng chē 'get in the car', 上班 shàng bān 'go to work'. Also 'last': 上個月 shàng ge yuè 'last month'.

example.english: The phone is on the bed.

hint: one syllable; able to, circumstances allow
note: Ability or possibility in the situation. In Taiwan it is heard most in the negative (不能 bù néng 'can't'); for requests people usually say 可以 kě yǐ. Compare 會 huì (learned skill) and 可以 kě yǐ (permission).
In writing also 她們 tā men (female) and 它們 tā men (things); all are pronounced tā men.
'Still' (還在 hái zài 'still here'), 'yet' with 沒 méi (還沒 hái méi 'not yet'), 'in addition' (還要 hái yào 'want more'). Other reading huán 'to give back' (還錢 huán qián).

gloss: to want to; to think; to miss
note: Before a verb it is a softer 'want to' than 要 yào. Before a person it means 'to miss': 我想你 wǒ xiǎng nǐ 'I miss you'.
Negates 有 yǒu ('don't have, there isn't') and past actions (我沒有去 wǒ méi yǒu qù 'I didn't go'). Often shortened to 沒 méi. Also a common short answer: 'No.'
Before a measure word often said nèi (那個 nèi ge). At the start of a sentence it means 'then / so': 那我們走吧 nà wǒ men zǒu ba 'then let's go'. The 'which' question word is the third-tone 哪 nǎ.
Makes a suggestion (走吧 zǒu ba 'let's go') or asks for agreement (你是老師吧 nǐ shì lǎo shī ba? 'you're a teacher, right?'). Other reading bā in 酒吧 jiǔ bā 'bar'.
Knowing a fact or information. Compare 認識 rèn shi (to know a person) and 會 huì (know how to). MOE lists both zhī dao and zhī dào; Taiwan speakers usually keep the 4th tone on dào.
讓 ràng + person + verb: 'let/make someone do': 讓他很生氣 ràng tā hěn shēng qì 'made him angry'. Also 'to give way' (讓位 ràng wèi 'give up your seat').

example.english: Let me think for a sec.

hint: short form, only before a verb or noun
note: Short for 沒有 méi yǒu: negates 有 yǒu and things that didn't happen; use 不 bù for habits and the future. Other reading mò 'to sink' (沒收 mò shōu 'confiscate').
把 bǎ + thing + verb: 'take X and do something to it': 把門關上 bǎ mén guān shàng 'close the door'. Also a measure word for things with handles: 一把傘 yī bǎ sǎn 'an umbrella', 一把鑰匙 yī bǎ yào shi 'a key'.
Also 'for / to' before a person: 打給我 dǎ gěi wǒ 'call me', 給你看 gěi nǐ kàn 'let you see'. Other reading jǐ in 供給 gōng jǐ 'supply'. Compare 送 sòng (to give as a gift).

After a verb it marks a continuing state: 門開著 mén kāi zhe 'the door is open', 坐著 zuò zhe 'sitting'. Other readings: zháo in 睡著 shuì zháo 'fall asleep', zhù in 著名 zhù míng 'famous', zhuó in 著陸 zhuó lù 'land'.
Very often said zhèi ge. Also used as a filler, like 'um', while thinking.
Same sound as 作 zuò in 工作 gōng zuò 'work'.
Asks or gives permission. As a reply it means 'sure / that works' or 'not bad'. Compare 會 huì (learned skill) and 能 néng (able).
Mostly heard in 為什麼 wèi shén me 'why' and 為了 wèi le 'in order to'. Other reading wéi 'to act as / be', in 認為 rèn wéi 'to think' and 成為 chéng wéi 'to become'.

gloss: to look; to watch; to read
note: Also 'to visit / see' (看醫生 kàn yī shēng 'see a doctor') and 'it depends' (看你 kàn nǐ 'up to you'). Other reading kān 'to look after' (看家 kān jiā).

example.english: Do you want to watch a movie?

note: After a verb it means 'have ever done': 去過 qù guò 'have been'. As a verb: 'to cross / pass / spend (time)': 過馬路 guò mǎ lù, 過年 guò nián. MOE gives guò; the mainland says unstressed guo for the 'ever' meaning.
Marks the passive, usually for something bad: 被罵 bèi mà 'got scolded'. Also means 'quilt' in 棉被 mián bèi. Other reading pī (literary).

example.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.
